Residual gap: Open heterogeneous MARL populations in energy environments
Justification: The MARL-oriented energy benchmarks reviewed support fixed agents, configurable populations, session dynamics, or heterogeneous predefined entities, but no included MARL benchmark demonstrated previously unknown agent types with new observation/action interfaces joining and leaving online. HELICS demonstrates this at co-simulation-federate level, not at learned-policy level.

Residual gap: Clear separation and benchmarking of session dynamics, asset availability and agent lifecycle
Justification: SustainGym, Chargym, CityLearn/EVLearn and EV2Gym all demonstrate why “EV enters/leaves” can refer to different abstractions. The literature/tooling does not expose one standard reconfiguration taxonomy or benchmark protocol across them.

Strong counterexamples exist for individual dimensions—large grids, configurable EV populations, vectorized simulation and GPU/JAX speed—but no common protocol found jointly measures population, heterogeneity, communication, reconfiguration, physical fidelity, training cost and inference cost.

Residual gap: Integrated REC + EV + grid-physics + heterogeneous-MARL benchmark
Justification: The components exist separately: CityLearn for communities, EV2Gym/SustainGym for charging, GridLearn/PowerGridworld for power flow, and CommonPower for safe heterogeneous control. The corpus did not reveal one mature benchmark combining all of them. Because the search was a scoping review without Scopus/WoS exhaustiveness, “moderate” is safer than “strong.”

HELICS already provides the underlying dynamic-federation and HIL mechanisms, so the gap is not infrastructure availability. The missing layer is a standardized MARL observation/action/lifecycle benchmark over that infrastructure.

Several environments have strong reproducibility mechanisms—CityLearn challenge datasets, EV2Gym replay, BOPTEST test cases, Grid2Op seed handling—but the definitions of seeds, stochastic session generation, environment configuration and physics differ substantially.

Residual gap: A standardized definition of an operational “digital twin” for MARL benchmarking
Justification: Some environments are data-calibrated or reproduce physical networks, while HELICS supports real-time/HIL integration. Whether the community needs a formal unified digital-twin benchmark is plausible but cannot be established strongly from this corpus alone.
